title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a10_legion

lines.sfx: A wood stove ticks in the corner of the Legion back room.
Mack Boone, fifty-five, the freight hauler who got them the contract, sets a thin folder on the card table and slides a sheet halfway out.
Cricket, Gunny, Stitch, and Dutch sit around the table with their coffee going cold.

lines.text: Read that before I say a word. Then you can throw me out if you want.

lines.sfx: Mack pushes the top sheet into the middle of the table.

lines.text: (reading) Lunar Heritage Neutralization Accord, artifact retrieval. Six containment units, class-A archival. Outbound configuration, empty.

lines.sfx: Dutch picks the sheet up and reads the whole of it through twice before he sets it back down.

lines.text: Six boxes. They go up empty.
And they come back down with the flags in them.

lines.sfx: Nobody says anything, and the stove ticks.
Mack turns the sheet over to a printed email and reads it off with no color in his voice.

lines.text: (reading) Containment units are non-crew hardware. No certification pathway required. Recommend sourcing retired fabrication and aerospace personnel at heritage-labor rates.

lines.sfx: He lays the page down where they can all see it.

lines.text: Heritage-labor rates. That's you, gentlemen. That's this whole room.

lines.sfx: Stitch turns his cup a quarter turn on the table.

lines.text: Cheap old men. To box up the—

lines.sfx: He lets it go, and not one man at the table takes it up for him.
Dutch already has the spec page out of his own packet and runs a thumb down the margin.

lines.text: This is my standard. The '98 archival spec. Word for word.

lines.sfx: Gunny stands and squares his chair back against the wall, and he stays on his feet.

lines.text: Somebody's going to fold those colors into them, on live television, with the whole world grading the job. I'd sooner it be men who know how a flag is handled than whoever else answers that email. We're the whoever-else, boys.

lines.sfx: A short, hard laugh goes around the table and dies out fast.
Mack deals a stapled packet to each man like he's dealing cards.
Papers riffle around the table, and only Dutch turns through the whole of his.
Mack taps the last page with one finger.

lines.text: No phones in the shop, no pictures. And whatever gets built in there, it stays inside those walls.

lines.sfx: Stitch signs his without turning past the first page.
Gunny signs, and Dutch signs under him, slow, down at the bottom of the last page.
Cricket slides his own packet back to the middle with no mark on it, puts his cap on, and gets up from the table.
The back door bangs shut behind him.
Out in the lot his boots grind across the gravel and go quiet.
Nobody moves, and Gunny pours a cup off the percolator he won't drink.
The gravel crunches again, the door opens, and Cricket comes back in with his cap still on.
He takes his packet up off the table, turns to the spec page, and reads it through standing where he is.
He picks up the pen and signs last, at the bottom, under Dutch.
